text:
Cale Makar is back. He missed three games on injured reserve with a soft-tissue injury, and coach Jared Bednar confirmed he returned cleared, no restrictions. Colorado needs him more than usual, with Nathan MacKinnon out.

Before the injury he was doing Makar things: 23 points in 19 games, 18 of them assists, and the Avalanche take 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 7.4 points better than without. His point rate (3.24 per 60) is running above even his own talent range, and he has five goals on 3.0 expected, so the scoring pace probably comes down a notch. Our range for the season is 69 to 94 points. The underlying game doesn't need luck: All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) has him at the 98th percentile among defensemen for chances from the slot. A Stanley Cup, a Conn Smythe and two Norris Trophies in, he is the one player Colorado can't replace while MacKinnon is gone.
